property_summary: For every admissible call to transfer(...) that does not revert, the reference contract always returns true; the mutant returns false for those same inputs, so there exist inputs where the mutant's return value differs (false) while the reference returns true.

For any admissible inputs where transfer(...) completes (does not revert), the reference C always returns true; the mutant returns false for the same successful calls, so there exist inputs where the returned boolean differs.

For any non-empty _tos array and any callee that always returns true on the encoded call, C.transfer never returns false (it always returns true); the mutant returns false whenever _tos.length > 1, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any non-empty _tos array and any callee that always returns success on the encoded call, C.transfer(...) always returns true; the mutant returns false when _tos.length > 1, violating this rule for some fuzzed _tos inputs.

For any inputs, contract C always forwards the first argument of transfer (the `from` address) as the first address argument in the external transferFrom call (i.e., the callee is invoked with (from, to, v)); the mutant swaps those two addresses and therefore for some inputs (when the callee's behavior depends on which address is first) the observable outcome from C differs.

For every input, the correct contract calls the external counterparty with the original `from` address as the first address argument of the transferFrom call (so when that callee only succeeds if its first address equals a specific expected address, C always succeeds), whereas the mutant swaps the two addresses and thus can cause the external call to fail for some inputs.

For every call to transfer(from, caddress, _tos, v) with a non-empty _tos array, the reference contract always reverts if any callee call fails (so the transfer call never silently succeeds when a callee reverts); the mutant removes the require on the callee result and therefore can succeed silently when a callee reverts, violating this rule for some inputs (a failing callee address and at least one _tos).

For any non-empty _tos array, the reference C always reverts (transfer call fails) if any callee invocation reverts; the mutant can succeed silently when a callee reverts because it drops the require on the callee's returned bool.
